definitions.explanation: A hand farming tool with a flat blade and a long handle, used to dig and turn over soil. Historically also a plow drawn through a field.

examples.japanese: {鋤|すき}で{畑|はたけ}を{耕|たがや}す。
examples.english: I till the field with a spade.

examples.japanese: {昔|むかし}は{牛|うし}に{鋤|すき}を{引|ひ}かせて{田|た}を{耕|たがや}した。
examples.english: Long ago, people had oxen pull a plow to till the rice fields.

examples.japanese: {鋤|すき}を{使|つか}って{土|つち}を{深|ふか}く{掘|ほ}り{返|かえ}すと、{作物|さくもつ}がよく{育|そだ}つ。
examples.english: When you use a spade to dig the soil over deeply, the crops grow well.

notes:
A traditional digging and tilling tool. The word is also part of the dish name すき{焼|や}き (sukiyaki), said to come from cooking on a spade-like metal blade.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {鍬|くわ}: hoe — has the blade set at an angle to the handle for chopping into soil, whereas a {鋤|すき} blade is in line with the handle for digging
- スコップ・シャベル: shovel — modern general-purpose digging tools
